text:
alex: quick sync — i'm proposing we treat the perimeter relay (the edge-facing proxy in customer VPCs) as a service-owned boundary rather than delegating ownership to customers. short list of tradeoffs below, pls react/reply.

sana: curious — is this primarily about operational burden or security isolation?

alex: both. operational: fewer on-call domains + consistent cert rotation. security: we centralize attestation and mTLS termination, which simplifies our control plane auth model.

lee: what about egress source IP preservation for customers who rely on fixed IPs? we get a bunch of asks for SNAT-preservation.

alex: two options: 1) preserve source using per-tenant egress bridges (more infra + IP pool mgmt) or 2) offer documented SNATed IPs from our managed pool + mapping logs. both supported but different SLAs.

priya: can we enumerate failure modes and automatic fallback? for example if relay can't reach CP, do we fail closed or route to regional fallback?

dan: i'd prefer fail-open to a degraded path for low-latency requests, but fail-closed for controlplane ops like model rollout or billing events. we should have a simple policy matrix.

alex: agreed. matrix sketch: controlplane-critical (SLO 99.9) => fail-closed w/ queued retries and operator alert; inference-data-plane => fail-open to regional relay or local cache with degraded SLA.

lee: important: TLS/cert model. if relay is service-owned we need automated cert distribution + short TTL rotation. customers asked for customer-provided certs in some regs. how do we support both?

priya: we can support two modes: service-managed certs (default) and customer-managed cert binding (enterprise opt-in). but that means we must design a clean interface for cert onboarding and periodic renewals.

alex: rough API for onboarding (informal):
```
POST /v1/relays
body: { tenant_id, cidr_allowlist, cert_mode: [service|customer], snat_preference }
returns: agent-install manifest + bootstrap token
```
we then rotate bootstrap token every 24h and issue long-lived node certs with 7d TTL refreshed via controlplane.

lee: token rotation every 24h could break air-gapped installs. need to support offline bootstrap (signed manifest) for on-prem.

priya: noted — add offline-signed-manifest flow where customer privately supplies a one-time signed blob and we accept intermittent outgoing heartbeats.

sana: ops impact: who owns the relay scaling? service or customer? auto-scaling inside customer VPC is a no-go for us (limits, IAM). pref: we operate a small managed pool per tenant with burst quotas.

dan: cost model concern — running many small managed relays increases cost vs. pushing customers to host. we should design a clear pricing/commit option for dedicated relay pools.

alex: yes pricing will be part of the enterprise contract. for self-serve tenants we allow customer-hosted relay image with our agent but limited SLA. enterprise gets managed relays + 24/7 support.

priya: logging & audit: we must ensure per-request provenance (relay-id, tenant-id, original-src-ip if preserved) and OTel traces. also maintain consented PII redaction when relaying payloads.

lee: implementation question: do we want the relay to terminate TLS and forward plain to CP (mutual TLS internal) or preserve TLS end-to-end with mutual TLS passthrough?

alex: prefer terminate+reestablish mTLS to allow inspection for QoS, routing, and caching. passthrough is an opt-in for regulated tenants.

sana: any constraints around VPC peering vs PrivateLink? customers with restrictive networking prefer PrivateLink. if we own relay, we can offer PrivateLink + managed endpoint attachments.

dan: note: PrivateLink has per-attachment costs — factor into pricing. peering requires cross-account roles; more ops but cheaper.

priya: action items I hear: 1) draft interface for onboarding + offline bootstrap 2) define cert modes + rotation policies 3) failure-mode matrix for controlplane vs dataplane 4) pricing proposals for managed vs customer-hosted relays 5) logging schema for provenance.

alex: yep. I'll spin up an RFC doc with those sections. can folks add concrete failure thresholds and example SLAs in the doc? cc @eng-infra @sre for ops constraints.

deploy-bot: scheduled: canary rollout of relay-v2 to staging at 23:00 UTC (no prod changes).

lee: one more nit — we need a compact health-check semantics for the relay so CP can triage: `{ status, last_seen, config_hash, cert_expiry }` as a minimal shape.

dan: +1. also add a mechanism to force remote debug on a given relay for 1hr with audit-log.

alex: perfect. i'll include health shape + debug policy. thanks all — will post RFC link by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
